answer: CRM cannot decide 'is it the same lullaby' as a matter of identity -- and it shouldn't try to. What it can do, and what I recommend the archive actually catalogue, is the evidence and the relation, leaving the identity question open for the cataloguer's own note. Each recording is a physical carrier (an E22 Human-Made Object/wax cylinder or tape) produced by a singing/recording activity (E7 Activity, with the singer as P11 had participant); what was sung on each occasion is documented as its own E33 Linguistic Object, carried by the physical medium via P128 carries -- this is squarely supported: E33's own scope note gives 'the free dialog in the local dialect recorded in 1958, Telemark, Norway stored on tape' as a worked example of exactly this kind of oral, dialect recording, and states that E33 treats an expression independently of the medium it happens to be captured on. Since the melody has simplified and two verses have dropped, the two performances do not have the same content, so they should be two distinct E33 instances, not one -- CRM's own instruction (Minimality: model only what's evidenced, not an assumed underlying abstraction) argues against forcing them into a single node. The relation between them is exactly what P130 shows features of exists for: its scope note explicitly covers 'siblings of a derivation process from a common source', and is symmetric when no single direction of influence is asserted, or directed (2003 recording -> 1952 recording) if the archive wants to record that the daughter's version derives from the mother's. That is the honest, supportable answer to the cataloguing question: 'distinct but related, and CRM lets you say so without committing to identity or non-identity of an abstract 'the lullaby'.' What CRM cannot currently give is a ratified class for that abstract, mutating 'the lullaby itself' persisting across variant performances. A class shaped exactly like that -- E100 Audio Item, explicitly 'independent of performance' -- exists in the CIDOC CRM 7.3.2 reference text, but it belongs to SIG Issue 274 'Archetypical sounds', which is still Open, its two properties are literal placeholders ('Pxx sounded', not a ratified number), and Martin Doerr's own reply in that debate separates exactly our situation -- 'sound as intangible heritage' -- as 'very different again' from what the class was designed for (recurring, near-identical sounds like a jingle, not drifting oral-tradition variants). The SIG's separate Issue 527 ('Modelling Provenance of Intangible Heritage', also Open) has Doerr naming this precise gap directly: music transmitted through variants 'may need a core-variant relation, or a variant set', unresolved as of that thread. And in an earlier thread on recording intangible cultural heritage, Christian-Emil Smith Ore states that for material 'transmitted from generation to generation' the SIG's own view is that FRBRoo, not CRMbase, is 'the most suitable ontology' -- and FRBRoo is outside what this search system indexes as a supported family model. So: catalogue the two recordings as related-but-distinct via P130 (fully in scope, well-evidenced); do not claim the model can adjudicate 'same lullaby' as a work-identity fact, because the SIG has explicitly not built that mechanism yet.

rejected_alternatives.option: E100 Audio Item (as the abstract, cross-performance 'lullaby')
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Appears in the CIDOC CRM v7.3.2 reference text with a scope note explicitly built for sound 'independent of performance', but it is tied to SIG Issue 274 'Archetypical sounds', status Open, with its properties still literal placeholders ('Pxx sounded'). Martin Doerr's own reply in thread t1467 separates 'sound as intangible heritage' from what that class targets, calling it 'very different again' -- it was designed for recurring near-identical sounds (a jingle, a bird call), not for content that drifts across an oral chain.

rejected_alternatives.option: Treating both recordings as one and the same E33 Linguistic Object
rejected_alternatives.why_not: The content differs (two verses dropped, melody simplified), so they are not the same documented expression; collapsing them into one node overstates what the archive actually has evidence for and contradicts Minimality.

Named by Christian-Emil Smith Ore in thread t0916 as the SIG's own preferred fit for material 'transmitted from generation to generation', but FRBRoo classes are not part of the family models this search system indexes (only CRMsci/CRMarchaeo/CRMgeo/CRMinf), so I cannot verify or cite specific FRBRoo classes through these tools.
